text: Good afternoon, everyone. It is 4:34 PM on Thursday, October 15th, 2026, and I call tonight's Student Services Committee meeting to order. I am John Pepper of the Dulles District. I am the chair of the Student Services Committee, and alongside me I have Ms. Carrie Labelle of the Catoctin District and School Board Chair, Ms. April Chandler of the Algonquin District.

We will begin this meeting with public comment. We currently have three speakers for public comment. I want to thank you all for engaging with this committee through the public comment process. The school board and the Student Services Committee welcome comments from Loudoun County residents, employees, and others with connections to our school system and believe that strong community engagement and outreach are important components of a successful school system. Speakers must limit comments to the time allotted.

Because we only offer 10 minutes for public comment in our committee meetings, each speaker will be allotted two minutes this afternoon. Please be advised that speakers who miss being called up will not be called at a later time. All audience members shall maintain civility, decorum, and respect for the function and dignity of this school board committee at all times. Please remain seated unless arriving, departing, or speaking.

Violations of civility, decorum, or respect include shouting, heckling, jeering, applause, or other noise which disrupts or delays the meeting, obstructing speakers from being able to see the committee or vice versa, interrupting speakers, attempting to speak when not called to do so by the chair, and/or approaching a speaker or otherwise attempting to intimidate, disparage, or distract a speaker, staff member, or other meeting attendees. Speakers should refrain from vulgarity, obscenities, defamation, profanity, or

other like breaches of respect, nor may speakers target, criticize, or attack individual students and/or individual division employees during public comment. Speakers should communicate those concerns to their school principal or other appropriate school official. The school board requests that comments on individual student or employee-related matter not be shared at public meetings where the disclosure could violate applicable confidentiality requirements. Speakers should face the committee and direct their comments to the committee.

Per LCPS policy 2520, members of the committee will not answer questions or respond directly to the public during the public comment period. Violations of decorum or civility of any meeting attendee may result in myself directing staff to remove the attendee from the remainder of the meeting. Copies of materials for school board members shall be given. They've already been given out to Mr. Dolson, who is the liaison to the committee.

Under no circumstances may a speaker approach the committee. All right. With that, we'll begin, and our first speaker this afternoon or evening is Carla Berman. And please forgive me one second. I am going to start a timer because we don't have the big timer for you. So I'll let you know when you're ready to start, and you're free to begin whenever you would like.

Thank you. Good afternoon. My name is Carla Berman. I'm the registrar at Willard Middle School. Wait. We're going to stop and let you start over. I'm just going to have you turn on your microphone. Thank you. Okay. Good afternoon. My name is Carla Berman. I'm the registrar at Willard Middle School. A group of registrars from across the county have worked on this document you've been given, this document. Several of us formed a group and have signed up to speak today, and we asked other registrars to join us to show support.

We're here to ask the board to review the classification of the position of registrar on the universal pay scale. We strongly believe that relative to other jobs in the county, the position of registrar is improperly classified. Over the past several years, responsibilities and technical demands of the registrar position have continued to expand, yet its placement on the pay scale has remained unchanged. During that same period, other positions within the division have received classification and compensation adjustments. We believe that this has created an inequity in which the compensation for

registrars no longer accurately reflects the significant level of responsibility, accountability, and specialized knowledge and technical expertise required for the position. The issue has negatively affected morale and we believe contributed to an ongoing turnover rate among registrars. Despite raising these concerns with HRTD on multiple occasions, the issue remains unresolved. We're therefore asking the school board to formally review the classification and compensation of the registrar position and determine whether an adjustment is

warranted. As registrars, our primary objective is to promptly and accurately register eligible students residing in our zone, ensuring seamless enrollment attendance. Navigating this process requires strict adherence to federal, state, local, and county-specific laws and regulations. There is detailed notes for all of those in what you've been provided. The responsibilities require registrars to exercise careful judgment, maintain a

high degree of accuracy while navigating situations that can have significant implications for students, families, schools, and the division. Unlike many administrative support roles across the division, registrars do not operate out of a quiet, dedicated office. We work directly from main offices and counseling suites and are fully integrated into daily building coverage. As a result, our time is continuously interrupted by general operational tasks that fall outside registration or record keeping. Thank you.

Our next speaker this afternoon is Martha Martinez. Good afternoon. My name is Martha Martinez, and I'm the registrar of Park View High School. Beyond the core registration and routine building operation that Ms. Berman discussed, our role requires ongoing management and especially academy record division program. Depending on the grade level, these critical

responsibilities include: attendance tracking, class scheduling, record transfers, alumni transcript processing, NCAL eligibility and formal audit, attendance, enrollment letters, graduation process, legal name change and adoptions, facilitated specialized registration of Head Start, ECSE, ESTET, IB, CAT, TNSS, Rise Academy, Academy Out Loud, Virginia

Virtual Distance Learning, VDLTJ, TAEP, ROTC, and HINCI, as well as supported dual enrollment and IP coursework. Executing accomplished legal requirement including FERPA compliance, subpoena fulfillment, Social Security background verification, discrete transcript

records management, VHSL athletic eligibility, junior guardianship, and Kinchi arrangement, foster care placement, and advanced technical operation and finance. Registrar more continually balance those technical and regulation responsibility with the immediately often and unpredictable needs in a busy school

office. Taken together, the registration position require an exceptional degree of multitasking, accuracy, discretion, technical knowledge, regulation awareness, attention to details. We believe that the great complexity and level of accountability associated with those responsibility are not adequately reflected in the position currently classified as compensation, especially in its comparison with the other position in the county. Thank you.

Our final speaker this morning is Shaquella Slaughter. Good afternoon. My name is Shaquella Slaughter. I'm the registrar at Madison Trust Elementary School. Continuing with Ms. Martinez's discussion of the comparison of our role to some others in the county, we want to highlight that unlike other administrative support positions, the registrar role uniquely requires a strong emphasis on compliance and funding, as data accuracy directly impacts state funding.

Other support roles do not carry regulatory or fiscal stakes. Far more student-family contact. We handle continuous face-to-face interactions in crisis situations, whereas other roles work with minimal interruptions. The management of complex technical systems, sensitive records, and unpredictable duties as assigned across multiple departments reinforce the scope of our position and the adaptability needed in the role. Another factor that is significant is the essential nature of position as evidenced by the fact that we're 12-month, year-round staff who report with snow days and routinely work without administrative oversight on site.

In summary, we respectfully ask the school board to consider the following facts. The unaddressed historical stagnation over the years surrounding support positions have been sys- Systematically reclassified, while the registrar position has remained unchanged despite continuous formal requests for alignment. The direct impact on district funding, the timeliness, precision, and audit compliance of our daily data management directly safeguards state funding for our schools. Our role as essential frontline representatives, as the primary liaison

for our schools, registrars interact daily with new and current families, school staff, central office personnel, and members of the public, frequently navigating sensitive family dynamics and most importantly, supporting students during immediate mental health crisis. The alarming turnover and associated financial cost for turnover rate registrars is astonishing and far exceeds the division's goals. Over the last three years, the turnover rate for this position reached 51%, averaging approximately 20% per year. Replacing and constantly retraining staff drains valuable time, administrative resources, and district dollars.

Many incoming staff are unprepared for the heavy technical demands of our job and expectations, leading them to leave the county or transition to higher paying, less demanding roles. The morale we are experiencing, those who have dedicated years to this role have repeatedly presented research, drafted revised job descriptions, submitted formal letters, met with school and central office administrators, and completed reclassification surveys where requested follow-ups just never occur. Watching colleagues leave school- Thank you. Sorry.

Thank you all for coming out and sharing your public comment and also sharing this letter with us. Appreciate the opportunity to engage with the public. With that, we will now-- Let me go back to my agenda, please. We'll now move into the item 3.01, which is the approval of the minutes from the September 17th, 2026 Student Services Committee meeting. May I have a motion? Ms. Chandler.

I move that we approve the September minutes for the Student Services Committee. Is there a second? I second. Thank you, Ms. Label. It has been properly moved and seconded. Is there any discussion or changes to the minutes of the September 17th, 2026 meeting? Seeing none, all of those in favor of approving the minutes from the September 17th, 2026 Student Services Committee meeting, please say aye. Aye. Aye.

That motion passes unanimously. Item four on our agenda, as always, is the presentation. Tonight's presentation is put together by our Director of Student Services, Mr. Kirk Dolson. And we will then move to our action item. Our first action item is item 5.01, revised policy 8140 on student attendance requirements and procedures. May I have a motion?

Ms. Chandler. I move that the Student Services Committee approve the student attendance requirements and procedures policy and move it forward to the full school board. Is there a second? I second. Thank you, Ms. Label. It has been properly moved by Ms. Chandler and seconded by Ms. Label. Is there any presentation, Mr. Dolson? Actually, yes, we do have Ms. Jennifer Evans here to provide you just an update.

Perfect. Thank you. Ms. Evans, the floor is yours. Good afternoon. I just wanted to walk you through the changes because last time we were here, we talked about additional recommendations from division council. One was just to restructure the policy to align with all of our other policies, so to have definitions. So you'll see on lines 45 through 62, we've just moved the definitions of an unexcused absence and a suspension

absence. And then as we discussed previously, adding in the active duty member of the uniform services and attendance concerns related to that, allowing students to have time away with their families who are experiencing deployment. And then we also expanded lines 104 where it talks about the absences for civic engagement, civic activities.

So that just we expanded that to be more than one day because often there are additional days that students will take. And I'll just open it up for questions. Committee members. Ms. Label. Yes, just for clarification, for students that may want to know this, what
qualifies as a civic event participation?

I don't have the answer to that because they're not often requested. Okay. But we'll look into that and get you that information. I think that might need to be part of the definition section just to clarify things. Yeah, and we do know that it's not supervised by LCPS staff. Yeah. So what we require is documentation that the student did successfully complete the civic engagement in order for that to be an excused absence, but we can definitely

get that information. Thank you. Ms. Chandler. I'm not sure that this is perfectly accurate, but for example, my daughter was just elected to go to the government, like Students in Government Day. So that may be an example of a civic engagement that would be appropriate since she is going to represent her school.

Okay. I'm going to ask a few questions actually about the civic engagement. As I read lines 108 to 110 in the redline version, I understand that it says prior advance notice of intended absence and documentation of participation in a civic event. It seems as if that is fragmented. There is no requirement on there. So

it says, if you read it in its entirety, backing up to lines 87 and 88, it says, "In addition, principals may excuse students who are absent for any of the following reasons." And then I'm going to scroll ahead and so, and it says, "Participation. Middle and high school students who engage in an optional civic activity or event not supervised by LCPS staff. LCPS shall excuse one school day long excused absence per school year and may permit additional excused absences for such students who

are absent for such purposes. Prior advance notice of intended absence and documentation of participation in a civic event." The phrase "are required" appears to be missing from this. Yes. We can add that. Okay. Appreciate that. My question is, what would be considered prior advance notice? So for example, I'm going to give you an example. A student might find out that a political candidate is coming at the last minute

for an event or rally and wish to attend, and that I would consider that a civic event. They may not have time to let the school know that they are in attendance, and might perhaps not necessarily have, they might get pictures from the family, but they might not have documentation. I would assume this would fall under that category. Yes. My question is, what is meant by, I guess we'll take this in two parts.

What is meant by prior advance notice? Is that defined in the policy? It is not, and one of the comments was about that's not always possible. And so there is flexibility around that. That is ideal to have prior advanced knowledge. But we didn't want to open that up so it's ever taken advantage of. But if a student and a parent is allowing their child to go to an event that is a civic engagement and they let us know that, we would just want that documentation after the fact. So sometimes things do come up like you described, and it's

tomorrow. So we would have the parent put in the absence in ParentVUE, say the rationale, and then we would just follow up with the documentation request. Okay. So I'm going to make an amendment, and I would like to add after the words "civic event" is, can we put the words is... I don't want to use the word required. I feel like required might be the important legal question here.

But I'm going to say is required when possible. For the documentation? For the documentation. For both the prior advance notice- How about upon request? ... is required. Maybe requested? Yes, maybe requested is actually the better way to do it. Maybe requested. Because we'll do that with absences related to medical illness. So we will say medical documentation may be requested. So let me make this in the right way.

I move that after the words civic event, we put the phrase may be requested. Do I have a second for my motion? Sometimes, right, just adding on to that one. Yeah. Second. Thank you, Ms. Chandler. It has been properly moved and seconded. Committee members, is there any discussion on this? Ms. Chandler. Well, Mr. Pepper, would you speak further to your motion?

I would like to, yes. Okay, so I'm adding this noting that when we're talking about attendance requirements, just in general, the proper recourse for an excused absence is to have it documented in some form. And sometimes we ask questions, right? If a student is absent for several days in a row for illness, we might ask for a doctor's note. Likewise, if a student is going to a civic event, we might ask for documentation.

Now, it's obviously not always possible, but this is just letting parents know you can't just say civic event and hope that students are excused. Even if you're saying, "Oh, they went to see a political candidate." I'm not going to give them off the top of my head here, but a political candidate speak, or they went to a forum or symposium.
Just knowing that LCPS has the capability to reach out and ask for further clarification, I think is something that parents should be expecting.

Do you require further clarification, Ms. Chandler? No, thank you. Okay. Ms. LaBelle. Thank you, Mr. Pepper. I think that it might be better said, "Prior advance notice of an intended absence should be given," because we're not asking for it every time. If it's last minute, as you say, should be given, "And documentation of

participation in a civic event is required." Does that do it for you? I do want to- They're two different things. Well, they are two different things, and I was trying to get it in one fell swoop. I almost want to say should be given where possible.

As soon as possible. In other words, if they wake up, they forgot to call last night, and they call. Thank you, then. In other words, if they wake up in the morning, realize that nobody called, they forgot, it slipped through the cracks, and they call and leave a message on the absences line, that would be as soon as possible. If they can do it sooner than that, that's wonderful. But if that's the last resort they have, then that's as soon as possible.

Okay. So do you want to- What? We have to make another motion. So we're on the first motion. Do you want to-- So we can- Play with the wording? We can play with the wording. However, it's going to require another motion. So I am okay with this, but I don't know if that's necessarily a friendly amendment because it's really changing a couple different things.

Well, I'm not growling at you guys. No, you're not. I'm trying to think of the logistical way in parliamentary procedure to get through this. So what I'm going to do is, I'm okay with the motion. What I would like to do, if that's okay with members of the committee, is withdraw my motion. Yeah. Okay. So I'm going to withdraw my motion, and Ms. LaBelle, I'm going to ask you to make a new motion that clarifies both pieces of this, if possible, one for the advance notice of the intended absence and one

for the documentation. And if you need a minute, I am totally okay with that. Nope, I'm good with it. All right, Ms. LaBelle, please proceed. Did you withdraw your motion? I withdraw my motion. Okay. Thank you. I would like to move that we make the change on lines 108, and 109, and 110, that prior advance notice of intended absence should be

given as soon as possible, and documentation of participation in a civic event must be documented. Second. Ms. LaBelle, can I make a friendly amendment instead of must be documented? Can we just change it to the words is required? Is required. Is that friendly? Yes. That's very friendly. You're not growling either. That's okay. Okay. Thank you. I second that. Okay.

Mr. Pepper. Ms. LaBelle, could you just repeat that so we make sure that we have all of-- You want me to read it for them, Ms. LaBelle? I'm happy to do it, but go for it, Ms. LaBelle. Oh, starting where it says, "Prior advance notice of an intended absence should be given as soon as possible, and documentation of participation in a civic event is required." Okay.

Thank you. Committee members, any further discussion on Ms. LaBelle's amendment? Okay. Seeing none. Did you second? I seconded it. Okay. All those in favor of the changes proposed by Ms. LaBelle, please say aye. Aye. Aye. That motion passes unanimously. We are now back to the original motion on the action item. Is there any further discussion on policy 8140? Ms. Chandler.

Thank you. In looking at the SEAC comments and concerns, I noticed that SEAC has raised a concern twice, related to the 15-day absences. Could you give me a little bit of context about why, I guess if this was raised in '23, and again, they still remain concerned about whether or not

the language federal and state disability laws would be appropriate. Could you just give us some context? Are there legal limitations that prevent us from including this? After 15 days of absences, we're required to withdraw a student. So their concerns, which I will share, did not come in until 10/12, so, we didn't have an opportunity to really look at those. But we handle every situation with care.

So if a student who has an IEP is withdrawn, we're doing everything in our power to reengage that family, get them re-enrolled, but we handle it by the code, which is after 15 days, it's a mandatory withdrawal. So we don't have that flexibility to do anything different with a student who has an IEP. So it is really a limitation of the code, and any of this clarifying language would not change our obligation under law. Correct. Okay. Thank you. Committee members, anything else?

All right. Seeing no further discussion, all of those in favor of moving this to the full school board as an information item at the next school board meeting, please say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. That motion passes unanimously. We will now move to our second action item, which is revised policy 5170 on substance abuse education. May I have a motion, please?

Ms. LaBelle. I move that the committee consider the motion 8140-- I'm sorry, 5170, substance use education, and move it forward in the process to our different committees. Ms. LaBelle, do you want a motion to the full school board? To the school board. We've done the committee work. Yeah. I'm sorry. It's okay.

To the full school board. Okay. Is there a second? Second. Okay. It was properly moved by Ms. Lavelle to move this to the full school board as an information item, and seconded by Ms. Chandler. Committee members, actually, I'm going to let Ms. Evans do this one as well, and do a quick presentation on 5170 before we get into discussion. This was the simplest change we could have. We just wanted to incorporate the addictive potential of electronic devices.

And I did want to let you all know that we do have a crosswalk in place with health and PE, and our substance use education program, to make sure that we're both touching on this. So we did have feedback from one student, which I truly appreciated. He said, "You can't just add an additional piece to a presentation," and that's not what we're doing. Mm. But I did appreciate his honesty and his feedback about our presentations.

And, again, we're touching on it in multiple ways through the collaboration with teaching and learning. Committee members, is there any further discussion? Ms. Chandler. The student's comment is fascinating, and always so pleased to hear from students. And I guess it resonates with me how much this is an important policy and an important change.

When it comes to the curriculum, ultimately, most of these things are outlined at the state level. Mm. But how does a program like D.A.R.E. come into play? So D.A.R.E. is separate from our curriculum. So our curriculum really is updated every year when we're looking at trends and what's happening, and we've included technology and social media as well. D.A.R.E.

has been in place for long before me. But it is something that we have developed an SOP to have consistency with how it's implemented. We're making sure that parents have that opt-out information, making sure they have the outline of what will be presented to their fifth graders. But it is something that we are collaborating with Loudoun County Sheriff's Office on, and we're hoping to have an agreement moving forward. But right now, it's not something we vet as LCPS.

It's law enforcement, and an agreement that's in place for them to come into our elementary schools. Thank you for that clarification. Mm. Do we anticipate that the change that's made to the policy will implicate, or how could it impact students on a day-to-day level? I don't see it really having an impact because we've already updated our

presentations and our lessons to touch on technology, gaming, gambling, all of the things that have been coming because of social media. That's great. All right. Thank you. Committee members, anything else? All right. Seeing no further discussion, all of those in favor of moving this to the full school board as an information item, please say aye. Aye.

Aye. That motion passes unanimously. We will now move into our information items. There is one information item tonight. It is on revised policy 8420 on student medication. And presenting that will be our Director of the Office of Student Services, Mr. Kirk Olson. Thank you, Ms. Pepper. With me this afternoon I have, or this evening, I should say, I have our Supervisor of Student Health Services, Ms. Jeanne Coleman.
I'm going to ask her to walk you through just some of the updates with policy 8420. I will turn it over to Ms. Coleman.

So, this change is just to align our policy with code. Ms. Coleman, can you just move the microphone a little closer to you? No, it's okay. I just want to be sure that the people that are listening on the recording can hear you. How's that? Perfect. Okay, good. The purpose of this addition to the policy is to just align the policy with Virginia code. There was a change to code that includes now

allowing students with a documented or with a diagnosed seizure disorder to carry their own rescue medication. And so we wanted to add that to our policy. It's for secondary students only, according to the code, and it gives them some flexibility moving around as they do from place to place, especially if they're running from school to work and they need to have that medicine with them.

It makes life easier for them and preps them for grown-up world. So as we look at what this actually looks like in practice, we would require, obviously, that the students have a seizure action plan in place, and then the possession permission would have to be something that we would also ask them to

sign off on, whether that be from a parent or if the student was 18, we would just need a doctor's order. And so, in this case, this is what we would add to the current policy. Any student enrolled in a secondary school who's diagnosed with a condition causing seizures may possess seizure rescue medications. Obviously, in the real world, having someone with epilepsy, they would not be able

to administer the medication. It would be there for an emergency purpose. Committee members, is there- We will certainly answer any questions that you might have ... any discussion or questions? I will say, in talking to Ms. Richardson about this policy, because of the change in state law, but the not updating of our current policy,

we're in this weird limbo situation where students who have any sort of seizure disorder are currently probably carrying their own medicine, but technically in violation of LCPS policy. And so we're in this weird gray area where I don't want any students who are in this situation to get in trouble for carrying their own medication. But I just want to make the committee aware that this is one of the things that we kind of have to push through relatively quickly because of this. Okay. So with that, and seeing very little discussion and limited changes, are we

willing to put this on consent at our next meeting? Or Ms. Chandler. I move to suspend the rules. Okay. I second. All those in favor of suspending the rules, please say aye. Aye. Aye. Okay.
